```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
## Network chunks run only when BacDive is reachable, so the vignette
## builds offline.
online <- tryCatch({
    httr2::req_perform(httr2::req_timeout(
        httr2::request("https://api.bacdive.dsmz.de/v2/fetch/24493"), 20))
    TRUE
}, error = function(e) FALSE)
## Use a temporary cache and settings, so building the vignette never
## changes the reader's own cache.
options(
    bdiver.cache = FALSE,
    bdiver.predictions = FALSE,
    bdiver.cache_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "bdiver-cache"),
    bdiver.config_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "bdiver-config")
)
```

# Introduction

[BacDive](https://bacdive.dsmz.de/), the Bacterial Diversity Metadatabase,
holds standardized phenotypic, physiological, and molecular data for more than
100,000 bacterial and archaeal strains. **bdiver** is a client for version 2
of the BacDive web service. It can

* search strains by taxon, culture collection number, or sequence accession;
* retrieve complete strain records;
* flatten records into tables with columns you choose; and
* export the whole database to a delimited file, for example to be used
    by [bugphyzz](https://bioconductor.org/packages/bugphyzz).

The BacDive API no longer requires registration. BacDive data may only be
used in compliance with the
[BacDive terms of use](https://bacdive.dsmz.de/about).

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("bdiver")
```

```{r load}
library(bdiver)
```

# Searching

Each search function returns the BacDive IDs of the matching strains.

```{r search, eval = online}
ids <- bdSearchTaxon("Phaeobacter", "gallaeciensis")
ids
bdSearchCultureCollection("DSM 26640")
bdSearch16S("KC176239")
bdSearchGenome("GCA_000511385")
```

Culture collection and accession searches accept several values, and can
match partially with `searchType`:

```{r search-type, eval = online}
length(bdSearchCultureCollection("DSM 2664", searchType = "startswith"))
```

# Retrieving records

`bdFetch()` downloads full records, 100 per request. Each record is a nested
list with one element per BacDive section.

```{r fetch, eval = online}
records <- bdFetch(ids)
names(records[[1]])
```

The rest of this vignette uses a record shipped with the package, so it can
also be followed offline.

```{r example}
record <- bdExampleRecord()
record$General$description
```

## AI-predicted traits

BacDive offers traits predicted from genome sequences by machine learning
models, such as Gram stain, motility, or oxygen tolerance. bdiver never
includes them unless you ask. For a single call, use
`predictions = TRUE`:

```{r predictions, eval = online}
predicted <- bdFetch(24493, predictions = TRUE)
names(predicted[["24493"]][["Genome-based predictions"]])
```

Predicted values appear in a `"Genome-based predictions"` section and also
next to observed values in other sections. They are recognizable by their
`confidence` score, and bdiver keeps them out of columns of observed
values unless asked to:

```{r predicted-values}
path <- c("Morphology", "cell morphology", "gram stain")
bdValues(record, path)
bdValues(record, path, predicted = TRUE)
```

To include predictions in every call, turn them on in your settings with
`bdPredictionsEnable()`; this is remembered in later sessions, and bdiver
reminds you when it is loaded. `bdPredictionsDisable()` turns them off
again, and `options(bdiver.predictions = TRUE)` turns them on for the
current session only. An explicit `predictions = TRUE` or `FALSE` in a call
always takes precedence. `bdSettings()` shows your settings:

```{r settings}
bdSettings()
```

# Building tables

## Fields

Any element of a record can be reached with a path of element names.
Because an element can hold one observation or many, `bdValues()` returns all
values found:

```{r values}
bdValues(record, c("Culture and growth conditions", "culture temp",
    "temperature"))
```

A *field specification* is a named list describing the columns of a table.
Each element is either a path, a field made by `bdField()`, or any function
that takes a record and returns a string.

```{r fields}
fields <- list(
    bacdive_id = c("General", "BacDive-ID"),
    species = c("Name and taxonomic classification", "species"),
    temperature = bdField(c("Culture and growth conditions",
        "culture temp", "temperature"), select = "first"),
    media = bdField(c("Culture and growth conditions", "culture medium",
        "name"), collapse = " | "),
    n_references = function(record) length(record$Reference)
)
bdExtract(list(record), fields)
```

## The result: a DataFrame

`bdExtract()` returns a `DataFrame` from
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("S4Vectors")`, Bioconductor's version of a
`data.frame`. It works like a `data.frame` (`$`, `[`, `nrow()`) and also
records where each column came from:

```{r dataframe}
tbl <- bdExtract(list(record), fields)
S4Vectors::mcols(tbl)
S4Vectors::metadata(tbl)
as.data.frame(tbl)
```

## Default fields

`bdDefaultFields()` gives the columns of the BacDive table used by bugphyzz.
Start from it and add or remove columns as needed:

```{r default-fields}
fields <- bdDefaultFields()
names(fields)
tbl <- bdExtract(list(record), fields)
t(as.data.frame(tbl))
```

`bdPredictionFields()` adds a prediction and a confidence column for each
predicted trait:

```{r prediction-fields}
preds <- bdExtract(list(record),
    bdPredictionFields(c("gram-positive", "motility")))
t(as.data.frame(preds))
```

# Exporting BacDive

`bdExport()` fetches records in batches, flattens them with a field
specification, and appends them to a file. Here, only a few strains are
exported:

```{r export, eval = online}
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
bdExport(out, ids = ids)
head(read.csv(out)[, 1:6])
```

Leave `ids` as `NULL` to export every strain in BacDive. IDs are then
scanned upwards from 1 until no more strains are found. A full export takes
about an hour.

## Interrupted exports

Rows are written to the file after every batch of 100 IDs, together with a
small progress file. If the export is interrupted (an error, a lost
connection, or R crashing), run the same call again: it continues where it
stopped, so at most one batch is downloaded again. With the cache enabled,
nothing is downloaded twice.

## Locks

While an export runs, a lock (`<file>.lock`) keeps other R sessions from
writing to the same file. It is removed when the export ends, even after an
error. If R crashes, the lock stays behind; the next `bdExport()` notices
that the process that made it has ended and replaces it.

On Windows, bdiver checks for that process with the `tasklist` command. If
it cannot check (for example when `tasklist` is not available, or the lock
was made on another computer sharing the same drive), `bdExport()` stops
and shows the lock's path. Make sure no export of that file is running, then
delete the lock and run `bdExport()` again:

```{r unlock, eval = FALSE}
unlink("bacdive.csv.lock", recursive = TRUE)
```

```{r export-all, eval = FALSE}
## Everything, in the bugphyzz format
bdExport("bacdive.csv")

## Everything, including AI-predicted traits
bdExport("bacdive_predictions.csv", predictions = TRUE)

## Selected columns as a tab-separated file
fields <- c(bdDefaultFields()[c("bacdive_id", "taxon_name", "ncbi_id")],
    list(keywords = c("General", "keywords")))
bdExport("bacdive_keywords.tsv", fields, sep = "\t")
```

# Caching downloads

bdiver can keep the records it downloads in a cache managed by
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("BiocFileCache")`. With the cache, records are
downloaded once and reused by later calls to `bdFetch()` and `bdExport()`,
whatever search they come from. This is useful when you

* run several searches and combine the results into one table;
* export again with different fields, without downloading BacDive again;
* work offline with strains you have already downloaded.

The first time bdiver downloads data in an interactive session it asks
whether to cache, and remembers your answer. You can also decide yourself
with `bdCacheEnable()` or `bdCacheDisable()`, or for one session with
`options(bdiver.cache = TRUE)` or `FALSE`. Here the cache is turned on:

```{r cache-enable}
bdCacheEnable()
```

For example, records from several searches can be combined into a
`DataFrame`; strains found by both searches are downloaded only once:

```{r cache-example, eval = online}
ids <- c(bdSearchTaxon("Phaeobacter"), bdSearchTaxon("Ruegeria"))
tbl <- bdExtract(bdFetch(ids, cache = TRUE))
dim(tbl)
```

Later, even offline, a table can be built from everything downloaded so
far:

```{r cache-offline, eval = online}
tbl <- bdExtract(bdFetch(bdCachedIds(), cache = TRUE))
dim(tbl)
```

`bdCacheInfo()` describes the cache; the same description is shown when
bdiver is loaded. `bdCacheClear()` deletes the cache.

```{r cache-info, eval = online}
bdCacheInfo()
bdCacheClear(ask = FALSE)
```

A cache of all of BacDive takes about 1 GB. Records fetched with
`predictions = TRUE` are cached separately.

## New BacDive releases

BacDive is updated in releases, and every record states the release it
comes from. `bdRelease()` returns the current one:

```{r release, eval = online}
bdRelease()
```

Cached records are kept until you decide to clear the cache, so your
results do not change unexpectedly. When bdiver is loaded in an
interactive session, it checks whether a newer BacDive release is
available and adds a line to its description of the cache. For example,
with a cache made before a new release:

```
bdiver cache: ~/.cache/R/bdiver
    19 strains (98.7 kB) from BacDive release 20251201.10
    Created 2026-01-12; last updated 2026-03-02
    A newer BacDive release (20260601.11) is available.
    To clear the cache, run bdCacheClear(). See ?bdCache for details.
```

The same notice is given the first time the cache is used in a session.
To move to the new release, run `bdCacheClear()`; records are then
downloaded again as you use them. Until you do, strains that are not in the
cache yet come from the new release, so a table can combine releases. The
release of a table is recorded in `metadata()`, and `bdExport()` reports it
when it finishes.

BacDive's web service does not send expiry information (`Expires` or
`Cache-Control` headers), which is why bdiver compares releases instead. To
skip the check, for example when working offline:

```{r keep-release, eval = FALSE}
options(bdiver.check_release = FALSE)
```

# Session information

```{r session}
sessionInfo()
```
